result:
**Changed (blocking):** the member-count near-miss decoy (previously `C_SIX`, 6 total members) was creating a real ambiguity — under the bot-excluded reading it had exactly 5 *human* members and would tie with the target. I replaced it with `C_FOUR` (4 total members, one short) instead of one over. Now the two possible readings of "5 members" no longer point at two different valid channels: under the bot-inclusive reading only `C_ATLAS` fully qualifies, and under the bot-excluded reading no channel satisfies all three conditions at once (the only channel with 5 human members, `C_GENERAL`, still fails on role and date). I also lightly reworded the request/explanations ("only has 5 members" instead of "exactly 5 members") for a slightly more natural, spoken feel and reordered the date clause before the count clause.

**Kept:** the multi-qualifier chaining style (owner + date + count in one sentence). Both provided expert examples (Box, Calendar) identify their target the same way — several precise conditions in one sentence, with no narrative preamble — so this is the established format for this pipeline, not a defect specific to my scenario. Rewriting it into a "just name the channel" style would go against how every scenario in this format works.
